title: Integrating the Multidimensional Index of Child Growth (MICG) with Stunting Indicators: An Implications for Indonesia
content: Background/Objectives: Stunting remains one of the most pressing public health problems worldwide, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, where children's growth is shaped by a complicated mix of overlapping factors. Indonesia has made some progress in recent years, but large disparities between regions still exist, and monitoring efforts still rely mainly on anthropometric measures such as height-for-age z-scores. This scoping review synthesized how the Multidimensional Child Growth Index (MICG) has been combined with conventional stunting indicators, and what this means for how child growth is assessed in Indonesia. Methods: Studies published between 2020 and 2026 that addressed multidimensional approaches to child growth and their relationship to conventional stunting measures were screened and synthesized based on predetermined eligibility criteria. Results: Six eligible studies conducted across low- and middle-income countries were included. The findings indicated that these studies were conducted in isolation and focused primarily on body measurements without considering results from multiple dimensions. Only a small number of studies revealed a co-occurrence between developmental delays and stunting. Conclusions: This review identifies a significant gap in operationalizing MICG within empirical studies, particularly in Indonesia, where multidimensional monitoring tools are not yet embedded in national systems. Integrating MICG into routine surveillance could enhance the identification of overlapping deprivations and strengthen policy relevance. Future research should prioritize validating MICG in LMIC contexts and developing integrated frameworks to support more comprehensive and equity-oriented child growth assessments.
